data.title: Multimodal AI
data.tagline: AI that can combine information such as text, images, audio, or video in one task
data.learningOutcome: You can separate input and output modes, decide what information to provide, and know what still needs verification.
data.description: Send a screenshot of a phone checkout page with the question “Why is the payment button missing?” and the AI can consider both the visible layout and your written question.

learning.assumes: You have sent text to AI and seen controls for uploading images, files, or recordings.
learning.outcome: You can separate input and output modes, decide what information to provide, and know what still needs verification.

explanation.title: A mode is a form of information
explanation.text: Text, images, audio, and video are common modes. Support for one does not mean support for all.

explanation.title: The same mode can be on either side
explanation.text: Audio can be input for transcription or output that reads an answer aloud.

explanation.title: Check the specific product
explanation.text: Supported inputs, outputs, and file types vary by model and product.

data.boundary: An upload control shows product interaction support, not necessarily a native multimodal model. Verify important results against the original source or real project.

lessonPractice.title: You want AI to explain why the payment button is not visible on a mobile checkout page. What is the best approach?

options.label: Attach the current screenshot, say where the button should appear, and ask it to separate visible evidence from causes that require checking the code
options.feedback: Correct. The image supplies the current screen, while the text defines the question and its limits. The model can inspect visible clues first; you, or an agent with project-tool access, must then verify the cause in the real project.

options.label: Only say “the page is broken, fix it” without a screenshot or a specific symptom
options.feedback: The model has neither the current screen nor a clear symptom, so it can only guess. A multimodal task still needs relevant information.

options.label: Upload only the screenshot and assume the AI can now see all code, hidden state, and runtime behavior
options.feedback: A screenshot contains only visible pixels. It does not automatically include source code, device state, or runtime data.

data.agentPrompt: This screenshot shows the checkout page on a phone. The payment button should be at the bottom, but it is not visible. First, use only the screenshot to identify any visible overlap or layout clues, and say when the image is not enough to confirm something. Then inspect the mobile layout in the project, fix the cause, and verify at the same screen size that the button is visible and clickable.
